title: Make The String Great
statement:
The string `s` is made of English letters in either case. Call two neighbouring characters a **clashing pair** when they are the same letter written once in lowercase and once in uppercase (in either order), such as `"aA"` or `"Bb"`; `"aa"` and `"AB"` are not clashing.

While the string still has a clashing pair somewhere, delete those two characters and close the gap. Return what remains once no clashing pair is left (this may be the empty string). Whatever order you delete pairs in, the final string is the same.
constraints: s contains only lowercase and uppercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

A deletion can bring two characters together that were apart, which can create a new clashing pair. The brute force rescans the whole string after every deletion, which costs O(n²). Instead, keep the characters that survive so far on a stack: the only character a new one can clash with is the one right before it, which is the top of the stack.

## Approach

1. Start with an empty `stack`.
2. For each character `ch` of `s`, look at the `top` of the stack.
3. If `top` exists, differs from `ch`, and is the same letter ignoring case, the two clash: pop `top` and drop `ch`.
4. Otherwise push `ch`.
5. Join the stack into the answer.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "leEeetcode"`. Push `l`, then `e`. Next `E` clashes with `e`, so pop: the stack is `[l]`. The next `e` is pushed, the following `e` matches exactly (same case), so it is pushed too. `t`, `c`, `o`, `d`, `e` are all pushed, and the result is `"leetcode"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each character is pushed and popped at most once.
- Space: O(n) for the stack.

## Pitfalls

- `"aa"` and `"AA"` do not clash: check `top !== ch` as well as the case-insensitive match.
- Removals can cascade (`"abBA"` vanishes completely), so a single left-to-right pass without a stack misses pairs.
- The answer may be the empty string; return `""`, not `null`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `stack` | characters that survive so far, in order |
| `ch` | the character being read |
| `top` | the last surviving character, or `undefined` |

narration.2: The stack holds the characters that have survived so far.
narration.4: Read the string one character at a time.
narration.5: Only the last survivor can clash with the new character.
narration.6: Same letter in a different case: the two form a clashing pair.
narration.7: Delete both: pop the survivor and do not keep ch.
narration.9: No clash: ch survives for now.
narration.12: The survivors, in order, are the final string.
